title: Add first-class encounter combatant state for monsters and NPCs
description:
The first combat playtest exposed that enemies are not addressable durable combatants. Bob's HP was updated correctly, but the near goblin could not be targeted by `adjust_hp`; the model tried several labels such as "near goblin", "goblin", "goblin-1", and "goblin-ambush", all failed, and the goblin's death was handled narratively / as lore instead of combat state. Combat needs a deterministic combatant model for monsters and NPCs.

Acceptance criteria:

- Starting an encounter can instantiate combatants from module encounter creatures.
- Each combatant has a stable id, display label, rulesRef, side/faction, HP, max HP, AC if available, conditions, alive/dead/unconscious status, and location/zone or encounter placement.
- Combatants can represent multiple creatures of the same type, e.g. `goblin-1`, `goblin-2`.
- A state mutation tool can update combatant HP and conditions. This may extend `adjust_hp` or introduce a combat-specific tool, but the target model must be unambiguous.
- Active combatants appear in the DM context with their ids and current status.
- The auditor can verify creature damage/death against combatant state instead of requiring improvised lore.
- Regression tests cover: two goblins ambush Bob; Bob damages `goblin-1`; Bob kills `goblin-1`; `goblin-2` remains active; invalid target labels fail clearly and suggest valid combatant ids; no goblin death is represented only as overlay lore when combatant state should exist.
close_reason: Implemented live encounter combatant state, start/update combatant tools, context/audit prompt support, schema migration, and goblin regression coverage. Verified with npm run verify:worktree.
